# Multi-Subject Medical Visualization

Also called: Multi-subject visualization

## Overview
Multi-Subject Medical Visualization is the visualization of datasets including measurements and imaging for more than one subject at a time [S1, unofficial]. It solves the problem of analyzing complex medical cohort studies where diverse data types must be integrated to diagnose or predict clinical outcomes [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by explicitly integrating heterogeneous data types (imaging vs. non-imaging) and coupling information visualization with scientific visualization techniques to extract patterns from the whole data collection [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The family relies on creating a highly interactive coupled view visualization interface [S1, unofficial]. This interface integrates both information and scientific visualization techniques [S1, unofficial]. The goal is to allow users to extract patterns and hypotheses from the whole data collection [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Mixed Modality Visualization](5716-mixed-modality-visualization.md)
Mixed Modality Visualization is the visualization of mixed modality data, including imaging, genetics, and blood measurements, acquired from a group of subjects. It solves the problem of analyzing complex medical cohort studies where diverse data types must be integrated to diagnose or predict clinical outcomes. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by explicitly integrating heterogeneous data types (imaging vs. non-imaging) and coupling information visualization with scientific visualization techniques to extract patterns from the whole data collection.

## Background
Medical visualization has started to work on the problem to work with multi subjects data. These datasets include measurements and imaging for more than one subject at a time. The aim of this paper is to be able to extract and analysis certain patterns that affect subgroups of the whole collection. LifeLines2, an early information visualization system to visualize and compare multiple patient histories or electronic medical records [S1, unofficial]. Work has been done on the interactive visualization of the multi subject and mixed modality datasets acquired by medical cohort studies [S1, unofficial]. In these studies, mixed modality data, including imaging, genetics, blood measurements, is acquired from a group of subjects in order to be anaylized for diagnosing or predicting the clinical outcome of that group.
